mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national ID issuing authority in the country of origin of the UBO/director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; where the country is not a Hague Convention party, consular legalization at a Canadian consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and business address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company, financial institution or government office in the UBO/director's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization; notarized English/French translation required where the original is not in English or French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or extract of corporate registry for each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the registry's jurisdiction or consular legalization at the Canadian consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or corporate authorization approving the formation of the British Columbia subsidiary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification by the corporate secretary and apostille by competent authority, or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every identified UBO, director, officer and 25% or greater shareholder against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, Canadian regulations under the United Nations Act, INTERPOL Red Notices, the Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act, applicable provincial securities and corporate disqualification registers, and commercial PEP and adverse media databases. Screening must be completed no earlier than 7 calendar days before the incorporation filing and documentary evidence of every screen must be retained for at least five years under Canadian AML/CFT record-keeping standards.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online - British Columbia Registrar of Companies (https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English and/or French using Latin script characters. The legal element must be a statutorily recognized word or abbreviation such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., Limited or French equivalents. The distinct element may be transliterated into French or English only when a faithful one-to-one rendering is provided and no confusion with an existing BC corporate name would result. Non-Latin script transliterations are accepted on the same basis, provided the name is set out in Roman characters on the BC Registry record.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Institute (when used to imply an academic institution)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name request is rejected, the applicant may submit an amended name reservation request with a new or revised distinct element and a further statutory fee. Alternatively, within 21 days of the rejection notice, a formal administrative appeal may be filed with the Director of the British Columbia Registrar of Companies, Vancouver office, stating the grounds of distinctiveness and demonstrating the absence of confusion with existing corporate names or trademark registrations. The Director generally issues a written determination within 14 business days. Further judicial review of a final adverse decision may be pursued before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A British Columbia business corporation must maintain a registered and records office at a physical BC street address capable of accepting service of process and mail during normal business hours. A virtual office provider that supplies a physical BC street address, mail forwarding and document storage may be lawfully used for a micro-SaaS business with no public-facing physical location. A post office box or non-street virtual address does not comply. The Registrar may require evidence of commercial substance where a single address is used to register an excessive number of companies or where service cannot be effected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection: approximately 3% for a single low-risk consumer micro-SaaS corporation with a dedicated BC registered office address. The likelihood rises to approximately 10-15% where a shared virtual office provider hosts multiple unrelated registrants on one street address, and is materially higher upon receipt of a regulatory complaint, an unexpected insolvency filing, or detection of suspicious service-of-process activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; estimated 2.5 hours at USD 180 per hour equivalent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57; ss. 10 (incorporation), 12 (corporate names), 27 (Notice of Articles), 117 (first directors), 124 (officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Corporate Online (CORES), Ministry of Finance
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; at least one share must be issued; no escrow or trust deposit required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation's share subscription and allotment be approved; that 100 common shares be issued to the incorporator upon receipt of the agreed subscription payment, subject to the Corporation's Articles. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation as set out in the Notice of Articles, British Columbia, be adopted and maintained pursuant to the Business Corporations Act. RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each holding office for one year or until successors are elected. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to execute filings, open banking accounts, and engage professional advisers. Dated at [City], British Columbia, this [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online (CORES) – British Columbia Registry Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access BC Corporate Online, complete the Name Reservation Request, and submit the statutory name approval criteria. Receive a reservation number valid for 56 days. If no name is desired, an incorporation will be numbered under the Business Corporations Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner rejects the name, submit a new name or file an objection letter within the prescribed review period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Notice of Articles and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles under the BC Business Corporations Act. Specify the authorized share structure, first director(s), and any special rights or restrictions. Obtain each director's signed consent to act.
required_dossiers: Signed Consents to Act as Director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Fields must comply with the Registrar's checklist; adjust wording and re-submit within the correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry (via BC Corporate Online or physical file at Victoria)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Articles, Articles, and consents with the BC Corporate Registry. Pay the incorporation fee. The Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation with the incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Consents to Act as First Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registry raises a deficiency, file a corrected Notice of Articles and Articles through the same portal within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Registered Office and Records Place
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office address is a deliverable physical address in British Columbia and that the Notice of Articles designates this address. Designate a records office where corporate books and registers are kept. No separate filing fee if set out in the Notice of Articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On query, provide proof of address and permission to use the premises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pass First Board Resolution and Appoint Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or circulate written consent resolution. Approve the issuance of shares to incorporators, adopt the registered office, and appoint the initial officers (e.g., President, Secretary, Treasurer). Record minutes in the corporate records ledger.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer declines, reappoint another individual by the same written resolution prior to filing any banking or regulatory forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Federal Business Number and Ancillary Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Certificate of Incorporation to register with CRA for a Business Number (BN), and open relevant program accounts (e.g., GST/HST, payroll if employees). The registration can be completed online in one session. Also monitor BC provincial tax registration requirements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA may issue a letter asking for clarification; provide the requested documentation within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (advisory only for office-based software activity)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No physical operating or manufacturing license required for a remote digital SaaS business

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy – Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – non-physical, office-based software service with no listed threshold under the Environmental Assessment Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no wastewater, air emissions, or industrial solid waste; office waste and electronic waste (WEEE) must be managed through municipal recycling programs

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance for office premises under the BC Fire Code; occupational health and safety clearance from WorkSafeBC; standard building occupancy permit required if the premises is leased

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - federal tax administration; electronic filing via Business Registration Online (BRO) and CRA My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses.html). British Columbia's 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is administered separately by the BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch, via the eTaxBC vendor portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate as a Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act (Corporations Canada online) or the British Columbia Business Corporations Act (BC Corporate Online) - no minimum capital; foreign ownership permitted. (2) Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) with program accounts: RT (GST/HST), RC (corporate income tax) and RP (payroll, if employees) through Form RC1 filed with CRA; the T2 corporation tax account is activated at incorporation. (3) GST/HST registration is mandatory once the 'small supplier' threshold (CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in the current calendar quarter or preceding four quarters) is exceeded; voluntary registration is available from the first dollar to claim input tax credits and to zero-rate export supplies. (4) For BC PST: register as a PST vendor in eTaxBC before making taxable retail supplies (including SaaS/licensed software) to BC consumers; BC has no PST registration threshold. (5) If Paddle or Lemon Squeezy acts as Merchant of Record (MoR / seller of record), the platform normally collects and remits GST/HST and PST on BC consumer sales; the entity should still maintain its own BN/GST account for direct supplies and document the MoR's principal role in the master services agreement. (6) A foreign-controlled Canadian corporation is taxed as a resident taxable Canadian corporation (ITA s. 89(1)); it is NOT a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), so the CAD 500,000 small business deduction and the reduced BC small business rate are unavailable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election: every incorporated entity is a taxable Canadian corporation taxed on worldwide income (ITA s. 2(1)); the only classification variants are CCPC vs non-CCPC (CCPC requires Canadian-resident control). Available elections relevant to this SaaS vehicle: (a) ETA s. 156 joint election - supplies between closely related registrants deemed made for nil consideration; (b) voluntary GST/HST registration election for small suppliers (ETA s. 240(1)); (c) corporate fiscal year-end election for a non-calendar T2 taxation year (ITA s. 249.1); (d) commercial MoR election appointing Paddle/Lemon Squeezy as principal to discharge consumer tax collection obligations. Hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.4 and 12.28) deny interest/deductions in connection with hybrid mismatch arrangements and provide no elective carve-out; the consumer micro-SaaS model with pure equity funding and no intra-group debt avoids hybrid structures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central bank); no dedicated foreign exchange administration exists; prudential supervision of banks and clearing systems is conducted by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money laundering supervision is conducted by FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for current and capital account purposes. Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, and there are no general exchange controls, surrender requirements, or Central Bank approval mechanisms for dividends, capital repatriation, or cross-border profit remittance. Dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-residents remain subject to Part XIII withholding tax (default 25%, potentially reduced under an applicable tax treaty) and must be reported on Form NR4. For capital transactions, the Investment Canada Act imposes a net-benefit review only for acquisitions of control of a Canadian business exceeding statutory thresholds; it does not restrict ordinary profit remittances or equity injections.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Canada. Exporters and cross-border SaaS providers may retain foreign currency in Canadian or offshore accounts without obligation to convert into CAD. All cross-border electronic fund transfers in excess of CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC, and exporters must maintain books and records consistent with the Income Tax Act and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low Feasibility. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) generally cannot lawfully provide Canadian-dollar clearing or deposit-like payment services to British Columbia residents without registering as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, where applicable, with the BC Registrar under the Money Services Business Act. Unregistered offshore EMI operations attract heightened scrutiny, often cause bank de-risking, and create legal exposure for the Canadian corporation. A viable route is partnering with a FINTRAC-registered Canadian MSB or using a regulated Canadian Schedule I bank that has an approved fintech banking partnership.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no absolute statutory mandate requiring in-person attendance for every corporate account opening in British Columbia; federally regulated banks may accept remote video identity verification where the verification is sourced from a reliable independent source and the bank documents the process. In practice, for a newly incorporated, non-resident-owned holding company with no Canadian business premise, the bank will almost always require physical presence of directors or a Canadian-based director/agent to complete the enhanced due diligence interview. Remote opening is possible but is materially accelerated by appointing a local director, a Canadian corporate service provider, or an in-branch corporate account manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership held through a multi-tier corporate or trust structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the certificate of incorporation, BC corporate registry search with filing history, a fully completed beneficial ownership register showing every individual with 25% or more entitlement, a Canadian legal opinion confirming the control structure, corporate chart, passports and government-issued identity documents of all directors, proof of residential address, source-of-wealth declaration, and an undertaking to update beneficial ownership information within 15 days of any change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder, director, or beneficiary located in a country weighted for money laundering risk or under sanctions scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening results, citizenship and tax residency certifications, a clear commercial rationale letter from the corporation, independent sanctions counsel opinion where required, evidence of the ultimate economic purpose (SaaS product, website, merchant-of-record payout statements), and a negative news/integrity report obtained from a reputable due diligence database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection arriving from a third-party account or without a clear source-of-funds trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the sponsoring shareholder showing the funds' original source, a signed share subscription or shareholder loan agreement, notice of articles and share allotment resolution, source-of-funds affidavit, tax documents (e.g., foreign tax return, tax clearance certificate), and any settlement statements from payment platforms (Paddle or Lemon Squeezy) if the entity is already in operational pre-revenue phase.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions or shareholder loans must be routed through a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer to the Canadian corporate operating account. The bank will apply name, reference, and sanctions screening, so the remittance instructions must identify the sending bank, the shareholder as the ordering customer, the Canadian corporation as the beneficiary, and include a clear narration such as 'Shareholder capital contribution pursuant to share subscription' or 'Due shareholder loan re capital structure'. The Payments Canada LVTSE framework applies for high-value domestic transfers once the funds arrive; no FX approval or purpose-code verification is required by the Bank of Canada, but the sending and receiving financial institutions must retain records for FINTRAC's EFT reporting threshold of CAD 10,000. A comprehensive funds-origin package, including the share subscription agreement, corporate resolutions, and source-of-funds evidence, should be delivered to the receiving bank before or with the wire to prevent holds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade-related disbursements and operational settlements, the permitted clearing rails include SWIFT MT103 for direct correspondent-bank transfers, commercial letters of credit (MT700 issuing and MT707 amendment flows) for documentary purchase transactions, and domestic payments via Payments Canada systems (LVTS, Real-Time Rail, or Automated Funds Transfer). For subscription software revenue collected through Paddle or Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record, payouts are typically consolidated and remitted by the merchant of record to the corporate bank account via SWIFT MT103 or an integrated payment rail. Refunds and supplier disbursements may be made via corporate procurement cards or AFT/EFT, subject to the bank's standard AML transaction monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) when the counterparty requires dollar settlement
Plain-vanilla foreign currency options (puts and calls on CAD)
FX swaps (exchange of principal at a near date and reverse exchange at a far date)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry (BC Registries and Online Services)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each anniversary of incorporation or recognition date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 100; continued non-filing may lead to strike-off and dissolution after approximately one year; directors may become personally liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal & BC combined)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; gross negligence penalty up to 50% of additional tax; interest accrues; criminal prosecution possible for habitual non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (eligible if annual taxable supplies under CAD 1.5M)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 250 minimum; additional penalties based on net tax; interest charged on unremitted amounts; enforcement and assessment actions may follow.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) for a private, non-distributing corporation; a company may waive appointment of an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution. Regulatory licensure or financial-institution status, if any, would trigger audit regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP – IFRS for public enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprise (ASPE) is the customary framework for a micro-SaaS private company. CRA requires books and records sufficient to substantiate tax filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual shareholder confirmation is filed under the BC BCA. However, the BC Transparency Register (Individuals with Significant Control) must be reviewed and updated within 15 days of any change and annually at year-end; it is available for law-enforcement and regulatory inspection upon request but is not filed with BC Registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required (waiver available); optional audit quote range 8,000-15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (combined federal 15% and British Columbia 12% general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction: federal 9% + BC 2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; SR&ED investment tax credits (refundable up to 35% for CCPCs); 10% provincial investment tax credit for qualifying activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (filed via CRA My Business Account or authorized tax preparation software)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., if FYE Dec 31, due June 30 of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from business operations (including SaaS subscription fees)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source revenue; if no permanent establishment, only Canadian-source income is taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (after deductions, loss carryforwards, and adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute based on Canadian-source income; apply treaty provisions if applicable.
Apply federal rate; consider small business deduction if eligible.
Allocate income to BC if permanent establishment exists; otherwise, may be nil.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance due plus 1% per month up to 12 months (max 17%); failure to file information returns (e.g., T5) incurs CAD 100 per day up to CAD 7,500; gross negligence penalty up to 50% of understated tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must provide Form NR-301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Treaty Benefits) and a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their home tax authority. The payer must withhold at the treaty rate (e.g., 15% for US under Canada-US Treaty) if the TRC is submitted before the dividend payment; otherwise, 25% is withheld and a refund claim can be made via Form NR-7.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%; treaty rates may reduce to 10% (e.g., US) or 0% for certain IP (e.g., software copyright). Interest: statutory 25%; treaty rates may reduce to 15% (US) or 0% for arm's length interest (e.g., US, UK).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for goods transactions and CAD 500,000 for services transactions with non-residents per year; below these thresholds, documentation is not mandatory but recommended.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like the UAE, but the CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and requires economic substance for treaty benefits. Transactions lacking commercial rationale or substance may be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting revenue, inflating expenses, or failing to file T2 returns to avoid tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239: fine up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties up to 50% of understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax under s.227.1 if they failed to withhold or remit; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a shell with no real business activity, employees, or assets, solely to obtain treaty benefits or avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may deny treaty benefits under GAAR; penalties up to 50% of tax benefit; potential criminal charges for fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for restitution and face civil fraud claims; travel bans and imprisonment up to 14 years under Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement AML compliance (e.g., no KYC for high-risk customers) or processing proceeds of crime through the SaaS platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: fines up to CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal charges for money laundering up to 10 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for AML failures if they knowingly participated; travel bans and asset forfeiture possible.
